about.title: Personal Injury Help in Upland, California
about.longDescription:
Upland sits where the foothills meet the western edge of San Bernardino County, and the roads that carry its 76,443 residents also carry a lot of pass-through traffic. SR-210 (the Foothill Freeway) runs across the north side of town. Euclid Avenue and Mountain Avenue move people north and south, and Foothill Boulevard cuts east to west through the retail core. In public collision records, those four corridors log the highest counts in the city. The 2025 numbers, the most recent final year, show 430 injury collisions in Upland, 628 people injured, and 2 lives lost. Reports tend to rise late on Friday afternoons, roughly 5 to 7 p.m., when commuters and weekend errands overlap.

If one of those collisions — or a fall, a dog bite, or a workplace accident — has left you hurt, the first steps can feel muddled. We handle personal injury claims throughout Upland and can help you understand your options. Our team works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You describe what happened; we tell you what your options look like. It costs nothing to ask.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Upland Claim

items.title: Two years, and sometimes far less
items.desc: California gives most injury claims a two-year filing window. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, a claim may be due in as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, being partly responsible reduces your recovery in proportion to your share but does not eliminate it.

items.title: No cap on pain-and-suffering damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no statutory ceiling on non-economic damages, so the human cost of an injury can be fully considered.

items.title: Contingency fees, not hourly bills
items.desc: We work on contingency. You owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Upland?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date of injury. Claims against a government entity, such as a city or county, can carry a much shorter window — sometimes just six months. Speaking with an attorney early helps make sure no deadline slips past.

items.question: Where do crashes in Upland tend to happen?
items.answer: Based on public collision records, the corridors with the highest counts are SR-210 (the Foothill Freeway), Euclid Avenue, Mountain Avenue, and Foothill Boulevard. These are neutral counts that reflect traffic volume, not a judgment about any particular road. Reports also tend to peak on Fridays between about 5 and 7 p.m.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule. Your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but you are not barred from recovering even if you shared some of the blame. We can help sort out how fault might be assigned in your situation.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to someone about my case?
items.answer: Nothing. We work on contingency, which means there is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case. You can ask questions and learn your options before making any decision.
